svg.title: Atomic structure overview
svg.desc: Elements, compounds, mixtures: Element: one proton number. Compound: elements chemically joined in fixed proportions. Mixture: not chemically joined. Balance equations with coefficients, never by changing formulae. Separate physically: Insoluble solid → filtration. Dissolved solid → crystallisation. Solvent → simple distillation. Miscible liquids → fractional distillation. Dyes → chromatography; pencil baseline above solvent. Particles & isotopes: Proton +1, neutron 0, electron −1. Atomic number = protons; mass number = protons + neutrons. Neutral atoms: protons = electrons. Ions gain/lose electrons. Isotopes differ in neutrons. Aᵣ = sum(mass × % abundance)/100. Electrons & models: First 20: shells fill 2,8,8,2. Same main group → same outer electrons; period → occupied shells. Scattering evidence → tiny positive nucleus, mostly empty space. Bohr: shells; Chadwick: neutrons. Group patterns: Group 0: full outer shell, unreactive; boiling point rises down group. Group 1: loses 1 electron; reactivity rises down group. Group 7: gains 1; reactivity falls. More reactive halogen displaces less reactive halide. Table & transition metals: Mendeleev left gaps and predicted properties; modern order is proton number. Transition metals: generally denser, stronger, harder, higher melting and less reactive than Group 1. Many form coloured compounds, variable-charge ions and catalysts.
